assessment: Five figures are the minimum coherent visual spine. The grid makes the row-column code and explicit reject output visible; the pipeline separates early spectral evidence from later temporal qualification; the coordinate comparison prevents exact-frequency correlations from being mislabeled as FFT bins; the duration band protects the named profile's 23-40 ms gray region; and the final ledger keeps coordinate choice, arithmetic units, latency origins, and the separate frozen receiver study auditable. None needs a sourced image or a frame sequence.
scope_guardrail: This is a synthetic course receiver, not a deployed telephone receiver, acoustic recording, reverberant-path study, or clipping study. The committed 101-tap 300-3400 Hz Hamming FIR is a course artifact and must not be labeled Q.24-compliant. The named receiver profile is the AT&T column in Q.24 Annex A, not a universal DTMF law. Exact nominal correlations, N=205 nearest bins, and N=256 nearest bins are three distinct coordinate sets. Arithmetic counts retain their declared real or complex units. Source-origin and received-signal-origin latency remain visibly distinct.

The five teaching claims are better served by original diagrams built from verified numeric data than by introducing an untracked keypad photograph or a copyrighted standards screenshot.

shared_conventions.ordinary_dft_coordinate: X[k]=sum_{n=0}^{N-1}x[n]exp(-j2pi kn/N); C(f)=X[k] only when f=kf_s/N
shared_conventions.profile: AT&T column of ITU-T Q.24 Annex A: operate offset <= +/-1.5%; non-operate offset >= +/-3.5%; high-minus-low twist -8 to +4 dB; operation duration >=40 ms; non-operation duration <=23 ms; pause >=40 ms; interruption <=10 ms
shared_conventions.palette: amber #e2903a for the active/example quantity, blue #4c8dd6 for the paired/support quantity, green #5aa46a for qualified output, and currentColor/opacity/dashes for scaffold and reject
shared_conventions.accessibility: Every distinction must survive grayscale through labels, outline style, dash pattern, shape, or position; do not encode accept/reject or row/column by color alone.

figures.brief_visual: Four-by-four DTMF row-column grid with key 5 highlighted and an explicit reject branch
figures.tier_reason: This is a fixed matrix with short labels, a single highlighted intersection, and one reject strip. Raw SVG gives precise alignment, works as the lesson key image, and needs no component behavior.
figures.source_status: original house construction from verified DTMF frequency and key mappings; no source image
figures.embed: <Figure src="./figures/dtmf-key-decision-grid.svg" alt="A four-by-four DTMF grid pairs low rows 697, 770, 852, and 941 hertz with high columns 1209, 1336, 1477, and 1633 hertz; row 770 and column 1336 intersect at key 5, while missing, duplicate, or failed gates lead to REJECT." caption="A key exists only at one qualified row-column intersection; every incomplete or conflicting pattern returns REJECT." />
figures.teaching_claim: DTMF decoding is a constrained one-low-plus-one-high decision with a first-class reject output, not merely selection of the two largest spectral values.

exact_data.worked_intersection: 770 Hz row plus 1336 Hz column -> candidate key 5
exact_data.accept_condition: exactly one qualified low-group tone and exactly one qualified high-group tone, followed by successful frequency, energy/dominance, twist, duration, pause, and interruption gates
exact_data.reject_condition: zero or multiple qualified tones in either group, or failure of any declared gate -> REJECT

figures.composition: Use a 640 by 420 viewBox. Put high-group frequencies across the top and low-group frequencies down the left. Highlight the 770 row in amber, the 1336 column in blue, and their key-5 cell with a green outlined confirmation mark. Route the full grid through a labeled gate bar to two terminal boxes, KEY and REJECT; keep REJECT equally visible, using an X and dashed outline rather than a warning color.
figures.mobile_and_theme: At 360 px preserve all eight frequency labels, all sixteen keys, the one-from-each-group rule, and both KEY and REJECT terminals. Remove secondary gate examples before shrinking labels below 11 viewBox units. Use currentColor and opacity with no baked background.
render_acceptance: The grid maps every key to the correct low and high frequency pair and highlights only 770 plus 1336 as key 5.
A lone tone, two tones from one group, or any failed gate visibly terminates at REJECT.
The graphic never says that the two largest magnitudes alone determine a key.
The figure remains legible at 360 px and in light and dark themes without relying on color.

figures.brief_visual: Feature-frame evidence and temporal qualification as two visibly different stages
figures.tier_reason: The pipeline contains equations, sentence-length gate labels, and two time bases that must stack on mobile. A hook-free component can use HTML and KaTeX for readable text while retaining a compact SVG timing rail.
figures.source_status: original house component from the repaired brief and corpus contracts; no sourced artifact
figures.embed: <Figure name="DtmfFeatureTimingPipeline" alt="A synthetic key-5 signal passes through the 101-tap course FIR, a 205-sample rectangular feature frame produces eight declared spectral coordinates, and a separate temporal state accumulates at least 320 received samples before frequency, dominance, twist, pause, and interruption gates can return KEY or REJECT." caption="Spectral evidence may arrive before temporal qualification; one 205-sample frame cannot by itself satisfy a 320-sample duration gate." />
figures.teaching_claim: A short spectral frame supplies evidence, while duration, pause, and interruption require state across frames; the receiver may emit a key only after both layers agree.

exact_data.course_fir: 101-tap symmetric Hamming difference-of-lowpasses, synthetic 300-3400 Hz course filter; group delay (101-1)/2=50 samples=6.25 ms; essentially flat at the eight DTMF frequencies
exact_data.feature_record: N=205 acquired samples at 8 kHz, rectangular window, 25.625 ms
exact_data.spectral_outputs: eight values from one explicitly selected coordinate family: either exact nominal C(f) values or declared FFT-grid bins; never a mixture
exact_data.temporal_minimum: 40 ms = 320 received samples for the named operation-duration gate
exact_data.other_profile_gates: pause >=40 ms; interruption <=10 ms; high-minus-low twist -8 to +4 dB; operate offset <=+/-1.5%; non-operate offset >=+/-3.5%

figures.composition: Across the top, show source, course FIR, one 205-sample feature frame, eight-coordinate evidence, and spectral gates. Beneath it, run a longer received-signal timeline with a persistent temporal-state box reaching 320 samples. Join the two lanes only at a final AND gate that has equally prominent KEY and REJECT exits. Show the FIR delay on a separate source-to-received origin bracket, not inside the 40 ms duration bar.
figures.mobile_and_theme: At 360 px stack the feature lane above the temporal lane and final outputs; preserve both numeric spans and the source-versus-received origin bracket. Use M/KaTeX, palette constants, currentColor, and no fixed background.
render_acceptance: The 205-sample frame is labeled 25.625 ms and is visibly shorter than the 320-sample, 40 ms temporal qualification.
The eight spectral values all belong to one declared coordinate family; the component does not mix exact nominal values with FFT bins.
The 6.25 ms FIR delay is measured between source and received origins and is not silently added to or removed from the received-origin duration gate.
No arrow permits a KEY output before both spectral and temporal gates pass, and every gate has a visible path to REJECT.

figures.brief_visual: Key-5 exact nominal frequencies beside their nearest N=205 and zero-padded N=256 FFT-grid coordinates
figures.tier_reason: Three aligned coordinate ledgers need exact formulas, signed errors, and responsive explanatory text. HTML tables plus KaTeX make the non-equivalence legible and auditable on mobile.
figures.source_status: original house component from independently checked arithmetic; no sourced artifact
figures.embed: <Figure name="DtmfCoordinateComparison" alt="For key 5, exact correlations evaluate 770 and 1336 hertz; the nearest 205-point bins are 780.4878 and 1326.8293 hertz, while appending 51 zeros gives nearest 256-point bins at 781.25 and 1343.75 hertz." caption="Zero padding samples a different frequency grid; neither nearest-bin pair is the exact-nominal correlation pair." />
figures.teaching_claim: Exact-frequency correlations and nearest FFT bins may both be useful receiver coordinates, but padding changes the sampling grid rather than converting a nearest bin into the nominal physical frequency.

exact_data.common: f_s=8000 Hz; acquired record N=205; key 5 nominal frequencies 770 Hz and 1336 Hz
exact_data.exact_nominal: C(f)=sum_{n=0}^{204}x[n]exp(-j2pi f n/8000), evaluated at f=770 and 1336 Hz
exact_data.n256_padding: append 51 zeros to the same 205 acquired samples
exact_data.interpretation: smaller bin spacing is a denser sampling grid, not new acquired information or automatically improved physical resolution

figures.composition: Use three aligned columns labeled exact nominal, N=205 grid, and N=256 grid. Give each tone one row with f or k, coordinate in hertz, signed error in hertz, and signed error in percent. Place a prominent not-equal separator between coordinate families and a 205 acquired plus 51 zeros brace above the N=256 column. End with the identity condition in KaTeX.
figures.mobile_and_theme: At 360 px stack the three coordinate cards while preserving the two tone rows, signed errors, and not-equal labels. The N=256 card must still state 51 appended zeros. Use KaTeX, palette constants, currentColor, and no fixed background.
render_acceptance: All four nearest-bin indices, coordinates, and signed errors match the frozen numbers.
The exact 770 and 1336 Hz evaluations are not given integer-bin labels.
The padded case says 205 acquired samples plus 51 zeros and never claims extra physical resolution.
The negative 1336 Hz error at N=205 and positive 1336 Hz error at N=256 are visually preserved.

figures.brief_visual: Named-profile duration number line with non-operation, gray, and operation regions plus 20, 25, and 45 ms fixtures
figures.tier_reason: A single one-dimensional band with three labeled regions and three fixture pins is a compact static plot. Raw SVG keeps boundary marks exact without putting sentence-length prose inside the asset.
figures.source_status: original house number line paraphrasing verified Q.24 Annex A AT&T-column values; no standards table or figure reproduced
figures.embed: <Figure src="./figures/dtmf-duration-profile.svg" alt="An AT&T Q.24 Annex A duration band marks at most 23 milliseconds as non-operation, strictly between 23 and 40 milliseconds as an unspecified gray region, and at least 40 milliseconds as the operation-duration region; fixtures at 20, 25, and 45 milliseconds fall into those three regions." caption="The named profile leaves 23-40 ms unspecified; the 25 ms fixture is not conformance ground truth." />
figures.teaching_claim: The named profile has two separate conformance boundaries, leaving an intentional 23-40 ms interval that must not be relabeled as mandatory accept or mandatory reject.

exact_data.profile_label: AT&T column, ITU-T Q.24 Annex A

regions.meaning: operation-duration requirement when all other gates pass

fixtures.label: duration gate passes; other gates still required

figures.composition: Use a 640 by 240 viewBox with a thick horizontal band and hard boundary ticks at 23 ms and 40 ms. Use a dashed outline and the word unspecified for the middle region. Place the 20, 25, and 45 ms fixture pins on separate vertical levels to prevent label collision; pair each millisecond value with its sample count.
figures.mobile_and_theme: At 360 px preserve both boundary values, all three region meanings, and all three fixture labels. Move fixture annotations above and below the band before reducing text below 11 viewBox units. Use currentColor, opacity, hatch/dashes, and no baked background.
render_acceptance: Exactly 23 ms belongs to the non-operation side and exactly 40 ms belongs to the operation-duration side.
The 25 ms fixture is labeled indeterminate or unspecified, never must reject or must accept.
The 45 ms fixture says only that the duration condition passes; it does not imply a decoded key without other gates.
The visual is a new number-line composition and does not imitate the source table's layout or wording.

figures.brief_visual: Ledger tying each coordinate choice to its arithmetic units, separating latency origins, and auditing the separate frozen receiver study against targets
figures.tier_reason: The comparison combines formulas, unit-bearing count rows, two latency origins, and a compact measured target ledger. A responsive component can stack these sections without turning caveats into tiny SVG text.
figures.source_status: original house component from verified arithmetic and timing contracts; no sourced artifact
figures.embed: <Figure name="DtmfCoordinateCostLatencyLedger" alt="A ledger compares exact 205-sample correlation and Goertzel costs with a 256-point FFT-grid cost, separates 40 milliseconds from received onset from the FIR's 6.25-millisecond source delay, and audits a separate 160-sample receiver study: clean and 10-decibel accuracy pass, while negative-control rejection and a 50-millisecond hard-set maximum latency fail their targets." caption="A fair comparison fixes coordinates, units, and latency origin; the frozen study passes two targets and exposes two failures." />
figures.teaching_claim: Algorithm choice is meaningful only after the coordinate set, operation unit, and latency origin are declared; a separate held-out target ledger then shows what the implemented receiver actually passed and failed.

exact_data.n205_exact_direct: eight exact nominal correlations over N=205: 1640 complex product slots and 1632 complex additions
exact_data.n205_exact_goertzel: eight real-input Goertzel evaluations at the same declared physical frequencies: 1656 real multiplications and 3288 real additions
exact_data.goertzel_guardrail: the recurrence must be implemented for the same possibly noninteger physical frequencies; do not silently replace them with integer DFT bins
exact_data.n256_selected_direct: eight selected coordinates over the declared zero-padded N=256 record: 2048 complex product slots and 2040 complex additions
exact_data.n256_radix2_fft: full radix-2 N=256 FFT: 1024 twiddle slots and 2048 complex additions; 1024 is not total work
exact_data.full_n205_direct_dft_reference: 42025 complex product slots and 41820 complex additions
exact_data.received_origin_duration: named operation-duration minimum 320 received samples =40 ms; actual decision latency also depends on state, block/hop alignment, and gate behavior
exact_data.source_to_received_filter_delay: linear-phase 101-tap FIR group delay 50 samples=6.25 ms
exact_data.source_origin_relation: source-origin latency must declare how FIR delay and frame/block alignment are included; do not publish 46.25 ms as an automatically exact total
exact_data.unit_rule: never sum real multiplications, real additions, complex products or twiddle slots, and complex additions into one unnamed total
exact_data.separate_receiver_study_label: frozen N=160 exact-nominal receiver study with 5 ms temporal blocks; not the N=205 or N=256 cost alternatives above

measured_target_ledger.metric: maximum accepted hard-set latency from received-signal onset

exact_data.study_denominator_guardrail: 24-39 ms gray-region trials and all training trials are excluded from conformance denominators

figures.composition: Use three coordinate cards: N=205 exact direct, N=205 exact Goertzel, and N=256 FFT-grid. Put every count in a unit-labeled row and draw an equality brace only between the two N=205 coordinate labels, not their heterogeneous work units. Beneath them, place two aligned timing rails: received-signal onset to temporal qualification, and source onset through the 50-sample FIR delay to the received origin. After a hard divider labeled separate frozen N=160 receiver study, show four target rows with literal PASS or FAIL, observed denominator/value, and target; use check/X shapes in addition to color.
figures.mobile_and_theme: At 360 px stack the three cost cards, the two timing rails, and then four full-width study rows. Preserve every operation unit, both latency origins, observed denominators, targets, and literal PASS/FAIL labels; remove the full-DFT reference row first if space is constrained. Use M/KaTeX, palette constants, currentColor, and no fixed background.
render_acceptance: The two N=205 methods are shown as computing the same declared physical frequencies, while the N=256 strategy is visibly a different grid.
Every count retains its real/complex and multiplication/addition/twiddle unit; no heterogeneous total or algorithm winner is displayed.
The N=256 FFT row reports 1024 twiddle slots and 2048 complex additions separately and never calls 1024 total operations.
Received-origin 40 ms and source-to-received 6.25 ms occupy different rails, and no universal or fabricated end-to-end latency is printed.
A hard divider labels the measurements as the separate N=160 study; no layout implies that N=205 or N=256 produced them.
The measured ledger shows two PASS rows and two FAIL rows exactly: 512/512, 1023/1024, 637/640 against 100%, and 50 ms against <=40 ms.
Gray-region and training trials are not included in any displayed conformance denominator, and no 17-by-17 confusion matrix is rendered.

rights_guardrails: Use only original house diagrams for the five planned figures; no sourced asset, screenshot, scan, or third-party keypad image is required.
Paraphrase the verified Q.23 frequency mapping and Q.24 AT&T-profile numbers. Do not reproduce Q.23 Figure 1, Q.24 Table A-1, their typography, wording, or layout.
Treat the official ITU PDFs as verification sources that may be cited or linked in References, not as permission to redistribute or adapt their visual pages.
Do not add a credit line to an original construction; preserve source citations in lesson prose and References for the numeric claims.
Do not use branding, handset photography, or standards logos as decorative filler.
nonvisual_contracts_for_writer: Name the AT&T Q.24 Annex A column every time its 23 ms, 40 ms, pause, interruption, offset, or twist values are presented as a profile; do not universalize them.
Keep the Q.23 sender tolerance of +/-1.8% distinct from the selected receiver profile's operate and non-operate regions.
State that the 101-tap filter and all evaluation audio are synthetic course artifacts and that the filter is essentially flat across the eight DTMF frequencies.
Do not attribute receiver-study metrics to the N=205 or N=256 audit alternatives: the complete study uses a 160-sample exact-frequency record and 5 ms temporal blocks.

If a confusion matrix is added in a later cycle, use only combined_conformance_heldout, preserve its frozen 17-label order and raw denominator 2176, exclude training and all 24-39 ms gray trials, and state the synthetic scope next to the figure.
Carry explicit KEY and REJECT outputs through prose, exercises, and any future implementation; no winner is a valid decision when any gate fails.
